chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazal, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The hostile one (Al-Nasibi) does not care whether he prays or commits adultery.
And this Verse was revealed regarding them:
Labouring, (hostile one) Entering into burning fire

key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: The hostile one (specifically those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'Amilat Nabisat' reveal about the Nasibi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the 'Nasibi' (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) are not merely sinners but possess a distinct theological status where their ritual acts, like prayer, are rendered void due to their core enmity, equating their spiritual state to that of a Zani (adulterer) in terms of validity. This hadith is traditionally linked to the revelation of Surah Al-Inshiqaq, where the term 'Nasiba' (hostile/laboring) is interpreted by Shia exegetes as referring specifically to the Khawarij or those who opposed the Imams. The implication is that external piety without internal allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt is insufficient for salvation.
